messages.subject: spurious lines in path plot
parts:
Hi!

I'm plotting 2 melted data frames in this way:
qplot(x=Time,y=Phase_Angle,data=S01RUE_SFEtablanrmmPH,geom=c("point","path"),color=k,facets=~variable)
x11()
qplot(x=Time,y=Phase_Angle,data=S01RUE_EFEtablanrmmPH,geom=c("point","path"),color=k,facets=~variable)

You can check the data here
https://sites.google.com/site/wolfydummysite/home/S01RUE_EFEtablanrmmPH.rda
https://sites.google.com/site/wolfydummysite/home/S01RUE_SFEtablanrmmPH.rda
and the 2 plots here:
https://sites.google.com/site/wolfydummysite/home/S01EFE.jpeg
https://sites.google.com/site/wolfydummysite/home/S01SFE.jpeg

Now I want to plot both graphics, one on top of the other. For this I'm doing
S01RUEtablanrmmJ = rbind(S01RUE_SFEtablanrmmJ,S01RUE_EFEtablanrmmJ)
then the plot:
qplot(x=Time,y=Phase_Angle,data=S01RUEtablanrmmJ,geom=c("point","path"),color=Jorang,facets=~variable)

You can check the data here
https://sites.google.com/site/wolfydummysite/home/S01RUEtablanrmmJ.rda

and the plot here:
https://sites.google.com/site/wolfydummysite/home/S01combi.jpeg

Two questions:
1. Why am I getting the straight lines in the third, combined plot? How can I get rid of them?
2. Is there any way to overlay the 2 initial plots instead of combining the data in one single data set?

Thanks!

--

> https://sites.google.com/site/wolfydummysite/home/S01combi.jpeg

> Two questions:
> 1. Why am I getting the straight lines in the third, combined plot? How can
> I get rid of them?

How would ggplot know from your data that you don't want a line
joining the last and first datapoints respectively from the two
datasets? You can add a dummy variable in your combined dataset that
indicates where it comes from, and use the group aesthetic.

> 2. Is there any way to overlay the 2 initial plots instead of combining the
> data in one single data set?

Yes, you can add a layer with a data argument,

ggplot() +
geom_path( ... , data = data1) +
geom_path( ... , data = data2)

HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: spurious lines in path plot
parts:
Hello Joan,

Following your examples, to get rid of the lines from the start to end I think you might want to add shape = k (or some other way to distinguish them).  Currently it treats both k values as part of the same series and gives you that line when it changes k values ( last point of k = 1 to the first point of k = 2).

qplot(x=Time,y=Phase_Angle,data=S01RUEtablanrmmJ,geom=c("point","path"), color=Jorang, shape = k, facets=~variable)

Cheers, 
Jonathan
